key_insight: Accelerating verifiable AI requires matching hardware and proof-system optimizations to workload-specific bottlenecks, not just speeding up isolated cryptographic operations.
engineering_relevance: Engineers must assess memory capacity, instruction issue and synchronization alongside execution time and bandwidth when selecting proof-generation hardware.
method: Review literature through four layers: AI workloads, proof systems, cryptographic kernels and hardware.
Measure six provers and seven kernels to identify practical cost drivers.
Assess hardware options and prioritize optimizations around measured bottlenecks.
evidence_signal: Across input lengths of 64–2048, fixed-weight commitment-opening costs stay nearly constant while intermediate-value work grows; a 13-billion-parameter fine-tuning configuration exceeds 40 GB GPU capacity but completes on an 80 GB device.
watch_item: Bottlenecks vary by proof system and input length, so isolated kernel speedups may not translate into end-to-end gains.
paper_title: Infrastructure for Verifiable AI: Where Proof Costs Go and How Hardware Can Help
